title: feat(lint): os validate, os build and os lint flag unread dashboard widget options keys by name
body:
Fixes #21131

Clause-②: yes

## What this does

`os validate`, `os build` and `os lint` now run `checkDashboardWidgetOptions` from `@objectstack/sdui-parser` over dashboard metadata (`*.dashboard.ts`, `defineStack({ dashboards })`). An `options` key that no renderer reads is flagged by name as `unconsumed-widget-option`, at the check's one level, `warning`. Until now the check had one caller, the SDUI tree validator (`packages/sdui-parser/src/validate.ts`), so a dashboard declared as metadata never met it, and `DashboardWidgetOptionsSchema` (`.passthrough()`) parsed any key in silence.

- **`packages/lint/src/validate-dashboard-widget-options.ts`** (new): an adapter, not a second check. It calls the check once per widget, with an array that holds only that widget at its own index, and turns each diagnostic into a finding at `dashboards[N].widgets[M].options`. Code, severity and message come from the check unchanged. ⛔ No key list: the read set is `CONSUMED_WIDGET_OPTION_KEYS`, which `check:widget-option-census` derives from the spec. The check's own exemptions (no `dataset`, legacy `component` widgets, expression-valued `options`, `suppressWarnings: ['unconsumed-widget-option']`) apply because the check is what runs.
- **`packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`**: one registry entry, `tier: 'advisory'`, `commands: ALL`, `input: 'parsed'`. The surface is CLI-only, and the `surfaceReason` says why: the per-write `dashboard` snapshot would carry its input, but crossing an advisory rule onto the Studio/REST/MCP door is a rollout decision over stored tenant rows.
- **`packages/lint/src/index.ts`**: exports `validateDashboardWidgetOptions` and `DashboardWidgetOptionFinding`.
- **`content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`**: the page stops teaching `icon`, `columns`, `striped` and `density` as working extras, and the `options` row stops saying "Renderer extras". A new table names the declared homes from `DashboardWidgetOptionsSchema`'s doc comment: the dataset measure's `format` and `currency`, the widget's `colorVariant`, and the widget's `chartConfig`.
- **`.changeset/21131-dashboard-widget-options-door.md`**: `@objectstack/lint` minor, with the `Clause-②: yes` line.

No CLI wiring was needed. All three commands call `runAuthoringRules` (`packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts`, `compile.ts`, `lint.ts`), and a registry entry reaches all three. That is measured below.

## The level: one check, one level

The check emits `warning`. The spec declares the bag open, and the ruling recorded in the check's header is that open extras stay open and stop being silent. This PR uses that same level at the new door. The triage pin says "refused by name"; here it is read as "flagged by name at that level", as the dispatch decided. `os validate --strict` does refuse it, because `--strict` treats warnings as errors. The measurement did not argue for a different level: the in-repo corpus writes zero such keys today (below), and PR #21130 removed the keys from the only producers the card names.

## Measured

Tree: `objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `5fb667f2` (code unchanged since `6b19d334`).

**Doors reached.** A throwaway probe built the CRM example (`examples/app-crm`) with `options: { icon, sortOrder }` written onto widget `total_pipeline` before `defineStack` ran:

| door | exit | `unconsumed-widget-option` findings |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `os validate` | 0 | 1, `severity: warning`, path `dashboards[0].widgets[0].options`, key `icon` |
| `os validate --json` | 0 | the same, in `warnings[]` |
| `os build --json` | 0 | the same, in `warnings[]` |
| `os lint` | 0 | the same |
| control: `sortOrder` (a read key) on the same widget | | 0 at every door |

The probe files were deleted after the run. The CLI prints "Running author-time rules (49)".

**Example corpus (assumption 4).** `os validate --json` over every example with a dashboard: `app-crm` 0, `app-todo` 0, `app-showcase` 0 (3 dashboards), `app-multi-package` 0 (no dashboards). So no example producer needed a fix. The other dashboard sources in the tree (`packages/platform-objects/src/apps/dashboards/system_overview.dashboard.ts` and the `create-objectstack` blank template) write no widget `options`.

**Tests.**
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 119 files, 5497 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit` clean, and `check:test-typecheck` OK (no new debt).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/sdui-parser test`: 13 files, 217 tests passed.
- New file `validate-dashboard-widget-options.test.ts` (8 tests). It pins the following:
  - An unread key is flagged with code `unconsumed-widget-option` and severity `warning`, and the finding names the key.
  - The control: all six consumed keys pass on a parsed widget.
  - Parity: the findings' code, severity and message equal the check's own diagnostics on the equivalent SDUI node.
  - The check's exemptions are honoured.
  - An id-less widget keeps its index.
  - `os validate`, `os build` and `os lint` each report it through `runAuthoringRules`.

**Ablation (one-time proof, committed state `6b19d334`).** `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced the check call with an empty diagnostic list. The anchor count went 1 to 0, and the blob went `e6339a78` to `4f3895a6`. Result: 6 of 8 tests red (every flagging pin plus the three per-command pins). The 2 green ones are the control and the exemptions, which assert an empty result. The restore was proven: blob equals HEAD `e6339a78`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

**Gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` at `5fb667f2` derived 89 families. All 89 were run at that head, every one exited 0, and `--ran` reconciled 89 derived, 89 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED. Notes:
- Three families first answered exit 3 (prerequisite not met). Each went to 0 once its prerequisite was met:
  - `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`: a shallow clone; fixed by fetching the pinned fixture commit.
  - `check:skill-examples`: needed `client-react` built.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`: needed the rest of the workspace built.
- `check:docs-transcript-drift` was red at first, a real finding: four CLI transcripts printed "author-time rules (48)". They now print 49 (see below).

## In-place corrections (declared)

- **`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, `deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`, `getting-started/build-with-claude-code.mdx`, `ui/react-pages.mdx`**: the transcript count went from 48 to 49. The new registry entry is what changed the derived count, and `check:docs-transcript-drift` holds these lines equal to it.
- **`content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`, the `stageOrder` row**: it said the key "parses and is never consulted" on a non-funnel type. The schema refuses it there (`checkDashboardWidgetStageOrder`, `packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts`). This is the same section and the same defect class (the page misstating what happens to an `options` key).
- **`content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`, the misspelling sentence**: it said a misspelled key (`sortDirection`, `granularity`) "is an author-time error". Measured: a `tsc --noEmit` probe in `packages/lint` against the built spec accepts `options: { sortDirection: 'desc', granularity: 'month' }` with no error. A wrong value for a declared key, `sortOrder: 'sideways'`, is TS2322 in the same run. The sentence now says the value is checked, while the misspelled key parses and draws this warning.

## Acceptance notes

- The fourth door (Studio, REST `/meta`, MCP publish) still does not run this check over dashboard writes. The entry records why in `surfaceReason`. Crossing it is a rollout decision.
- `DashboardWidgetOptionsSchema`'s doc comment (`packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts`) still says a typo such as `sortDirection` "is now an author-time type error". The `tsc` probe above measures that as false. Fixing it is a `packages/spec` TSDoc edit (`check:docs` regeneration), which this PR leaves to whoever next edits that file. The docs page here no longer repeats the claim.
- The finding's message is the check's own text, which opens with the host type in angle brackets (the SDUI node spelling). The `where` field carries the metadata location next to it.
- The skill sentence (`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md`) is a governed surface. It goes in its own docs-only PR, part of the same card.
